thread:
sara (docs): Quick note — I opened PR to reconcile examples after the invoke wire change. https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4680 Please help with snippets, migration notes, and a tiny 'reject-and-explain' guardrail example.

leo (sdk): On it. I'll replace legacy examples that access `function_call` top-level and add a compatibility shim. Suggest a short safe helper: `safeFirstText(outputs, fallback)` to keep snippets tidy.

mike (runtime): FYI hosted already returns invoke_v2 by default; Dedicated clusters can enable `compat-mode`. Important: the canonicalization change affects signature verification for signed tool manifests — on-prem customers will need to re-sign.

anya (qa): I'll produce three test payloads: compact v2, expanded schema envelope, and a validation-failure case. Posting curl+responses to the PR so docs examples can reference them.

zane (pm): Partner demo on Fri — we need migration command + one-liner that Ops can paste. Also a short blurb on latency delta when switching from compat to v2 (even a sentence is fine).

sara (docs): Proposed structure: 1) short v2 quickstart 2) migration checklist (redwoodctl + curl) 3) guardrails: strict vs permissive patterns 4) SDK snippets (TS/PY safe helpers) 5) troubleshooting (signed manifests, empty outputs).

leo (sdk): Draft TS snippet I'll push: 
```ts
// safe helper
function safeFirstOutputText(resp){
  return resp.outputs?.[0]?.text ?? (client.config.compatibility ? resp.function_call?.args?.text : null);
}
const res = await client.invoke('translate', {text: 'hola'});
const text = safeFirstOutputText(res);
```

mike (runtime): Small request: wrap the `function_call` access behind `if (client.config.compatibility)` and mark it as a temporary shim — don't present it as best practice. Also add note about `x-kv-cache` header being best-effort and may be absent in compat responses.

anya (qa): In compat-mode I saw `outputs: []` while `function_call.name` existed but `args` was empty. I'll add that as an 'unexpected empty outputs' test case and include the relevant runtime log lines. Docs should recommend checking signed manifest validity and runtime logs for that symptom.

sara (docs): Good — I'll include a troubleshooting bullet and a sample log snippet. Also adding a one-line `redwoodctl` command: `redwoodctl cluster set-invoke-compat --cluster my-prod --enable`. Mike, confirm exact flag?

mike (runtime): Confirmed. Exact CLI: `redwoodctl cluster set-invoke-compat --cluster <name> --enable`. For on-prem KMS customers, add re-sign command: `redwoodctl tools resign-manifest --cluster <name> --manifest ./tools.json`. Link to support: https://redwood.ai/support.

zane (pm): Nice. Also add a short migration note for SDK users: bump client to v1.8.0+ to get the `compatibility` flag in config.

leo (sdk): I'll update the snippet header to note `client v1.8.0+` and include both TS and Py helper implementations. Pushing soon and will run `docs-ci check-links`.

sara (docs): For guardrails section, I'm adding two patterns: 
- strict: validate JSONSchema, return 400 with friendly message, log `schema_validation`
- permissive: try fallback parsing, emit a warning metric, and surface human-readable explanation.

anya (qa): I'll attach the curl artifacts and expected outputs. Please don't merge until QA confirms docs examples match staging runtime.

sara (docs): timeline: aiming to merge after QA signoff tomorrow noon. I'll add a short PR checklist in the description.

sara (docs): Thanks everyone. PR checklist I'll drop in PR: update TS/PY snippets, add migration redwoodctl + curl, guardrail examples, troubleshooting log sample, KMS re-sign note, attach QA artifacts, hold merge until QA green. Reviewers: leo/mike/anya.

zane (pm): Thanks team  this saves the partner demo.

sara (docs): merging after QA ack. :pray:
